Give Your Game a Memory — Variables and Lists

Create the "brain" of your quiz with variables and data lists

What we're doing: Now we create the "brain" of our quiz. Variables store single pieces of information (like your score). Lists store whole collections (like all the image paths and all the answer choices).

🧩 Analogy A variable is like a labelled jar — you write score on the label, and whatever number is inside the jar is your current score. A list is like a numbered shelf. And a list-of-lists? That's a whole bookshelf — each shelf holds another row of items!

A) Create Three Variables

  1. Open the Variables category in the toolbox
  2. Click Create variable... → name it score
  3. Drag set score to 0 into the Setup section (after m5ui.init)
  4. Repeat: create current_round, drag set current_round to 1 into Setup
  5. Repeat: create high_score, drag set high_score to 0 into Setup
💡 Why does current_round start at 1? Because UIFlow2 lists count from 1! When we ask for get item 1 from images, it gives us the first picture. So our round counter should match — round 1, image 1, answers for round 1. No messy +1 offsets needed!

B) Create the Images List

  1. Open the Lists category. Drag create list with into Setup, name it images
  2. Click the gear ⚙ on the block, add slots until you have 8, and fill them:
    "Q1.jpg" "Q2.jpg" "Q3.jpg" "Q4.jpg" "Q5.jpg" "Q6.jpg" "Q7.jpg" "Q8.jpg"

C) Create the all_answers List (a List of Lists!)

  1. Drag another create list with block, name it all_answers. Click the gear ⚙ to add 8 slots (one per round).
  2. Inside each slot, drag another create list with block with 4 text items. Fill them like this:
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ all_answers (the bookshelf — 8 shelves) │ │ │ │ Shelf [1]: ["Olm", "Newt", "Frog", "Axolotl"] ← R1 │ │ Shelf [2]: ["Mars", "Venus", "Jupiter", "Saturn"] ← R2 │ │ Shelf [3]: ["Statue of Liberty", "Tower of Pisa", ← R3 │ │ "Big Ben", "Eiffel Tower"] │ │ Shelf [4]: ["Woodrow Wilson", "Theodore Roosevelt", ← R4 │ │ "Herbert Hoover", "Franklin D. Roosevelt"] │ │ Shelf [5]: ["Haiti", "Puerto Rico", "Jamaica", ← R5 │ │ "Dominican Republic"] │ │ Shelf [6]: ["The Sylvers", "Jackson 5", ← R6 │ │ "Earth, Wind & Fire", "The Osmonds"] │ │ Shelf [7]: ["Chanel", "Comcast", "Channel 4", ← R7 │ │ "Coca-Cola"] │ │ Shelf [8]: ["Rose", "Tulip", "Orchid", "Hyacinth"] ← R8 │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
💡 What's a list of lists? It's like a bookshelf! The outer list (all_answers) is the whole bookshelf with 8 shelves. Each shelf holds another list of 4 books (the answers for one round). To get the answers for round 3, you pull out shelf 3 into current_choices, then pick the book you want. No tricky multiplication maths — just two simple lookups!

D) Create the correct_index List

  1. Drag a third create list with block, name it correct_index, add 8 number slots:
    4 4 1 2 3 2 1 4
💡 What's an index? In UIFlow2, lists start counting at 1 — so the first item is index 1, the second is index 2, the third is index 3, and the fourth is index 4. The correct_index list stores which answer is right for each round using these index numbers.
✅ What you should see: In your Setup section, you now have three set var to value blocks (for score=0, current_round=1, high_score=0) and three create list with items blocks (images, all_answers, correct_index). Your quiz now has a memory!
💾 Save your progress! Your quiz has a brain now! Next we'll teach it how to set up each round.
